add_widget.description: Add a widget to a dashboard (requires write permission). For text widgets: use 'content' (not 'html') as the config key. For bigNumber widgets: dataPoints need 'name' field, include 'bigNumberItems' array, colorThresholds use 'relation'/'threshold', aggregateFunction is lowercase (e.g., 'average'). For cgraph widgets: deviceDisplayName/deviceGroupFullPath/instanceName must be GlobMatchToggle objects {'value': '...', 'isGlob': true}, dataPoints need 'display' object, graphInfo needs 'aggregate': false when using topX. For deviceSLA widgets: required config fields are 'groupName' (not deviceGroupFullPath), 'deviceName', 'dataSourceFullName', 'metric', 'threshold'. Also required: 'daysInWeek' (e.g., '1,2,3,4,5,6,7'), 'periodInOneDay' (e.g., '0:00-23:59'), 'displayType' (0=availability, 1=timeline), 'calculationMethod' (0=percent, 1=actual), 'unmonitoredTimeAlertStatus' (0=ignore, 1=warning, 2=error, 3=critical).

analyze_alerts.description: Analyze one alert window: call this for how many alerts fired and when, which alerts belong together, how noisy alerting is, which datasources burst, or which portal changes preceded a spike over the last hours. One read of the window's active and cleared alerts, under the severity, device, group and datasource filters, feeds every section; 'statistics' gives active and cleared totals, counts by severity, the ten busiest devices and datasources, and the volume of each hour, cleared alerts included; 'clusters' groups two or more alerts by device, by datasource and by signature (datasource and datapoint), with their alert ids and first and last start times, and a device cluster names the device_id its alerts share, null for a website or two devices under one name; 'noise' gives a 0 to 100 score from the entropy of alerts over datasource and datapoint (weight 40), flaps, an alert on the same device and datapoint that re-fires within 30 minutes of clearing (30), and repeats, a combination with three or more alerts (30), with the first ten flap pairs and tuning recommendations; 'bursts' gives the windows of window_seconds on one datasource that hold at least min_alerts alerts on min_devices devices; 'changes' reads the audit log once and pairs each change (a create, update, delete or import, read from the entry's description) with the first 5-minute alert spike, a bucket above the mean by one standard deviation, within correlation_window_minutes after it, with a confidence from 1.0 to 0.5. truncated says when the 5000-alert cap cut either read short. Use get_alerts to list or page through the alerts themselves.

correlation_window_minutes.description: Longest gap from a change to the spike it pairs with (default: 30)

datasource.description: Only alerts from datasources whose name contains this, regardless of case

device.description: Only alerts on devices whose name contains this

group_id.description: Only alerts on devices in this device group

hours.description: Hours the window reaches back from now (default: 24)

min_devices.description: Fewest distinct devices a burst holds (default: 3)

analyze_blast_radius.description: Count the devices a device failure could reach through topology neighbors: neighbor_count at depth 1, dependent_count beyond it, each device's alert status, and critical path devices. A device whose neighbors neither topology path answers is listed under unreadable with a warning, never counted as zero; on a portal without those routes every read is unreadable.

analyze_metric.description: Analyze one device instance's metric series, such as CPU, memory or disk usage: call this for statistics on a datapoint's recent history, such as its current level against the window, whether it is rising, its daily cycle, when it shifted, or which samples stand out. One paged read of the window feeds every section; 'summary' gives latest, mean, standard deviation, min, max and the latest sample's signed z-score; 'trend' gives least-squares and Theil-Sen slopes per hour, r-squared, coefficient of variation, the detrended 24-hour autocorrelation and a label (volatile, cyclic, increasing, decreasing or stable); 'seasonality' gives detrended autocorrelation at 1, 4, 12, 24 and 168 hours, the dominant period and the peak hours in UTC; 'change_points' gives level shifts, where the mean of the next 30 samples leaves the mean of the previous 30 by five times the noise in that comparison (measured with any steady trend and autocorrelation the noise has), with the daily cycle removed first when the window holds three days or more and that leaves less noise; each shift has its timestamp and the levels before and after it, less the daily cycle when that was removed. A change in the last 30 samples is not reported yet, small shifts in strongly autocorrelated noise go unfound, on a window under a day a change inflates the noise and smaller shifts go unfound, and changes about a day apart in a few days leave the cycle in and go unfound; 'anomalies' gives z-score, IQR and MAD hits, each method's 20 most extreme; 'forecast' gives the least-squares and Holt-Winters (daily season, two days of samples needed) slopes per hour and, with threshold, when each crosses it, within 30 days; 'baseline' compares the window with one as long ending baseline_hours_ago hours ago (one more read): both windows' statistics, the mean's percent deviation and a status (normal within 20 percent, elevated or reduced within 50, anomalous past it). The baseline runs only with baseline_hours_ago. Use get_device_data for the raw samples.

analyses.description: Sections to compute (all if omitted; the baseline only with baseline_hours_ago)

baseline_hours_ago.description: Hours before now the baseline window ends, such as 168 for the same window a week earlier

threshold.description: Level the forecast reports the crossing of

ask_edwin.description: Ask Edwin AI a question in plain words and wait up to 120 seconds for its answer. Edwin investigates with its own tools and returns `answer`, `reasoning` (its tool-call narration), a `conversation_id` to pass back for a follow-up, and `truncated: true` when the answer stopped early. Slower than the get_edwin_* reads; use it when a question needs Edwin's judgment rather than one of its records.

conversation_id.description: A conversation to continue; omit to start one

audit_network_monitoring_coverage.description: Portal audit that counts UPS/PDU devices onboarded, interface DataSources applied, SNMP credentials configured, and NetFlow exporters set up. calculate_availability.description:
Calculate availability percentage from alert history. Computes SLA-style uptime metrics, MTTR, and per-device breakdown from the window's cleared and active alerts, read as two lists; truncated says when the 5000-alert cap cut either read short. With target_slo it adds error_budget for the window: budget, consumed and remaining minutes, percent consumed, burn rate, projected exhaustion in days and a status (healthy, warning past 50 percent, critical past 90, exhausted).

Common mistakes: hours_back defaults to 720 (30 days). Narrow scope with device_id/group_id for performance.

group_id.description: Optional device group ID filter; not with device_id or device_name

severity_threshold.description: Minimum severity for downtime (critical, error, warning, info)

target_slo.description: Target availability percentage, such as 99.9; adds error_budget over the hours_back window

capacity_plan.description: Composite capacity planning: reads each instance once through analyze_metric to classify its trend, detect seasonality and change points, and forecast when it crosses threshold (default 90). Summary rows carry each forecast method's breach_eta (epoch seconds) and hours_until_breach per datapoint.

datasource.description: Filter to a specific datasource name

device_name.description: Device display name (used if device_id not provided)

threshold.description: Level each forecast reaches for, in the datapoint's unit (default: 90)

clear_session_context.description: Clear all session context (variables and history)

collect_device_config.description: Trigger an on-demand config collection for a device instance

correlate_metrics.description: Compute Pearson correlation between multiple metric series. Joins the series by timestamp bucket, as wide as the coarsest series' median sample interval with finer series averaged into it, and correlates over the buckets every series holds, reported as shared_samples. Builds an NxN correlation matrix and highlights strong correlations (|r| > 0.7). Maximum 10 sources.

sources.description: List of metric sources to correlate

detect_site_outage.description: Composite workflow for site outage detection. Chains CollectorDown detection, mass-interface-down burst analysis, UPS on-battery events, and downstream device silence into a single site-outage verdict with confidence score, scope, and affected device list. Designed to catch the class of site-outage that generic AIOps correlation misses. Pass a device group ID representing the site.

group_id.description: Device group ID representing the site. Devices in this group define the analysis scope.

hours_back.description: Context window for power events in hours

diagnose.description: Composite diagnosis: given an alert, or a device's latest open critical alert, gathers the alert details, device context, alerts clustered and audit changes in the last four hours, blast radius, and the device's assigned DiagnosticSources with the latest results of the alert's diagnostic runs. It reads those results and never runs a DiagnosticSource. It computes no health score or root cause; health_check reports each metric's z-score.

device_name.description: Device name to diagnose (finds most recent critical alert)

edwin_run_tool.description: Run one tool on one of Edwin AI's MCP servers, sending `parameters` to Edwin unchanged. Requires write permission: an Edwin tool can change the systems it connects to, and this server cannot tell which tools do, so every run is gated and audited. Take mcp_name and tool_name from get_edwin_tools; the parameter names come from the tool's short_description, since Edwin publishes no input schema. A tool that reports failure returns REJECTED_BY_TOOL with Edwin's error.

get_audit_logs.description: Read the portal audit log: call this for who did what and when. kind='all' returns one page of entries, newest first; kind='change' returns the configuration changes (create, update, delete or import, read from each entry's description) found in a pool of the newest entries, with scanned and has_more; kind='login' returns portal sign-ins, sign-outs and failed logins, one query per login wording (up to six calls), with status and method per row, success_only or failed_only, and total as a lower bound while has_more is true; kind='api_token' returns the rows naming an API token, given by access_id or token_id (read to its access ID), keeping only that exact access ID, with event (change, rejected, throttled), path and method per row. username is an exact name or a comma-separated list; action and resource_type (kinds all and change) are whole words the description holds (the portal applies one, the second is matched on the fetched page); start_time and end_time bound the entry time in epoch seconds. System and automation actors (System:*, LogicMonitor Internal, cloud auto-delete) are dropped after the fetch for kinds all and change unless exclude_system is false or a username is given; dropped counts them and paging follows the rows the portal returned. An argument another kind reads is refused. offset plus the rows read must stay within 10,000, and the filter within about 900 characters.

access_id.description: With kind api_token: the token's whole access ID

action.description: Whole words the description holds, e.g. Action=Delete

change_type.description: With kind change: the change type to keep

end_time.description: Only entries at or before this epoch second

exclude_system.description: Drop system and automation actors (default true)

failed_only.description: With kind login: failed logins only

kind.description: all: every entry; change: configuration changes; login: portal logins; api_token: rows naming an API token

resource_type.description: Whole words the description holds, e.g. Type=Device

start_time.description: Only entries at or after this epoch second

success_only.description: With kind login: successful logins only

token_id.description: With kind api_token: the token's id, read to its access ID

username.description: Exact username, or a comma-separated list

get_device_properties.description: Get all properties of a device (resource)

get_device_property.description: Get a specific property of a device (resource)

get_devices.description: List devices (resources) from LogicMonitor, optionally filtered by name, hostname, status or device group

filter.description: Raw filter expression (overrides other filters). Syntax: field:value, field~value. String values must be quoted: displayName~"server". Custom property queries use dot-notation: customProperties.name:"env",customProperties.value:"prod"

hostname_filter.description: Filter by hostname or IP address (substring match)

get_diagnostic_remediation_assignments.description: List the diagnostic and remediation sources assigned to a specific resource or alert (Automated Diagnostics & Remediation). Unlike get_diagnosticsources/get_remediationsources, this resolves which modules actually apply to the target.

module_type.description: Restrict to one module type (both if omitted)

get_diagnostic_remediation_results.description: Get structured execution results for diagnostic and remediation source runs: status, trigger type, executor, script output, and timing. Provide exactly one of alert_id or host_id. Time window params are epoch milliseconds; result timestamps are epoch seconds.

cursor.description: Diagnostic-side cursor from a previous response (not valid with module_type "both")

diagnostic_source_id.description: Filter to one DiagnosticSource by ID

diagnostic_source_name.description: Filter to one DiagnosticSource by name

remediation_cursor.description: Remediation-side cursor from a previous response (not valid with module_type "both")

remediation_source_id.description: Filter to one RemediationSource by ID

remediation_source_name.description: Filter to one RemediationSource by name

get_diagnosticsource.description: Get details about a specific DiagnosticSource including datapoints

raw.description: Return the full REST object, the definition create_diagnosticsource takes, instead of the summary

filter.description: Raw LM filter expression (overrides typed filters). Operators: : (eq), !: (neq), ~ (contains), !~ (not contains).

get_edwin_alert_volume.description: Count the alerts Edwin AI received in the last `hours`, by hour or by alert state. Returns [key, count] buckets, hour keys in epoch milliseconds, and Edwin's total for the window. The Edwin credential needs the query_aggregate scope; without it the call fails with SCOPE_MISSING naming that scope.

group_by.description: Bucket by hour of creation or by alert state

hours.description: Window in hours back from now

get_edwin_insight.description: Read one Edwin AI insight by its `_id` from get_edwin_insights, with every field Edwin holds for it, including the ones get_edwin_insights leaves out. Each epoch-millisecond timestamp comes with an ISO 8601 twin.

insight_id.description: The insight's _id, such as correlation_<uuid>_<epoch ms>

get_edwin_insights.description: List the insights Edwin AI created in the last `hours`, newest first. An insight is an incident Edwin built by correlating alerts. Each row has Edwin's id and display id, state, workflow state, severity, causal CI, impacted CIs, alert count and alert keys, a link into Edwin, and once Edwin has analyzed it, its title, summary, root cause, impact, timeline, remediation, evidence, contributing factors and similar incidents. Call this to find what Edwin concluded about an incident before reading raw alerts and metrics; get_edwin_insight reads one insight whole. `total` is Edwin's count of matches; it has read exactly 10000 for a window of all time, so treat 10000 as a lower bound. A cleared insight reads severity 0.

causal_ci.description: CI Edwin named as the cause, matched exactly

hours.description: Window in hours back from now, on the insight's creation time

impacted_ci.description: CI that must be in the insight's impacted list

severity.description: Edwin severity numbers (ml.insightSeverity) to match any of; a cleared insight reads 0

state.description: Insight state to match exactly; active and cleared are the values seen

get_edwin_metadata.description: List Edwin AI's record types with their field counts, or with `record_type` the fields of one type, so you can name fields in get_edwin_records filters and columns. The extra.* fields, the CI's LogicMonitor properties, are counted but not listed unless `prefix` asks for them.

prefix.description: Only fields whose name starts with it, such as extra. or cf.

record_type.description: Record type to describe, such as alerts; omit to list the types

get_edwin_records.description: List Edwin AI's own copy of the alerts or events it received in the last `hours`, newest first unless `order` says otherwise. Use it to see what Edwin correlated; LogicMonitor's alerts are read with get_alerts and insights with get_edwin_insights. `filter` takes one Edwin filterCondition condition, ANDed with the window, such as {"EQUALS": [{"type": "string", "field": "cf.eventCI"}, "web01"]}; get_edwin_metadata lists the field names. Without `columns` every field comes back except extra.* (the CI's LogicMonitor properties) and raw.* (the source record).

columns.description: Fields to return beside _id; name extra.* or raw.* fields here to get them

filter.description: One filterCondition condition, ANDed with the window

hours.description: Window in hours back from now, on meta.createdTimestamp for alerts and meta.eventTimestamp for events

get_edwin_tools.description: List Edwin AI's agents, or with `agent` (such as LMDiagnosticsAgent) that agent's MCP servers and the active tools on each. The mcp_name and tool name pairs are what edwin_run_tool takes. Edwin publishes no input schema for its tools, so a tool's short_description is the only guide to its parameter names.

agent.description: Agent name; omit to list the agents

get_escalation_chain.description: Get details about a specific escalation chain

raw.description: Return the full REST object (every field the API returns) instead of the summary

get_graph_data.description: Get graph image data for visualization

get_integration.description: Get a specific integration's full definition. Field set depends on integration type; password/OAuth secret fields are masked.

get_integrations.description: List LogicMonitor integrations (Custom HTTP Delivery, Slack, PagerDuty, etc.). Returns a short summary per integration.

type_filter.description: Exact-match filter on the integration type, e.g. 'http' for Custom HTTP Delivery, 'slack-2', 'pagerduty'. Wildcards are not supported for type.

get_interface_metrics.description: Pull interface-level metrics (in/out bytes, errors, discards, utilization, status) for a device's interface over a time window. Answers 'how is this port performing?' Resolves the Interface-family DataSource and the instance matching the interface name before fetching datapoints.

metrics.description: Comma-separated datapoint names. Defaults to RxRate, TxRate, ErrorsIn, ErrorsOut, DiscardsIn, DiscardsOut, InterfaceStatus.

get_link_flaps.description: Identify interfaces with repeated up/down transitions in a time window. Answers 'which ports are unstable?' Common causes: bad cable, duplex mismatch, bad SFP, PoE power cycling, WAN instability.

device.description: Scope to a device name (substring match)

interface_pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matching interface DataSource names

min_transitions.description: Minimum alert fires to qualify as flapping

get_ops_note.description: Get details about a specific ops note

contains.description: Substring filter on metric names (wildcards unsupported)

get_power_events.description: Filter alerts for UPS/PDU power-event signatures across APC, Liebert, and Eaton DataSources ('on battery', 'runtime remaining', 'input voltage lost') over a time window. Returns events matched by DataSource or alert name substring with counts per pattern.

device.description: Scope to a device name (substring match)

patterns.description: Override default patterns. Default covers UPS, PDU, APC, Liebert, Eaton, Battery, PowerSupply, Power_.

health_check.description: Composite health check: resolves a device, picks up to five of its datasources whose names mention CPU, memory or disk (drive, volume, filesystem), reads the first instance of each through analyze_metric (summary and anomalies over 24 hours), checks open alerts, and calculates 30-day availability. A device with none of those datasources gets an empty metrics list and a warning.

device_name.description: Device display name (used if device_id not provided)

ingest_logs.description: Ingest log entries into LogicMonitor (requires LMv1 auth)

logs.description: Array of log entries to ingest

portal_overview.description: Shift-handoff overview of the portal: reads the alert window of the last hours_back hours once for statistics, clusters and noise, and lists the collectors and the active SDTs. detail_level=full adds up to 20 open critical and 20 open error alerts from across the portal, not only the window, and up to 20 dead devices; summary does not read them.

push_metrics.description: Push custom metrics into LogicMonitor (requires LMv1 auth)

metrics.description: Metric payload with resource mapping and datapoints

query_otlp_metrics.description: [PREVIEW] Run a PromQL range query against native OTLP metrics. Returns a time-series matrix

query.description: PromQL expression. Examples: container_memory_usage_bytes (raw series), avg(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total) (aggregate), rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total[5m]) (per-second rate), nginx_up{service_name="api"} (label matcher). Discover names and labels with get_otlp_metric_names / get_otlp_metric_labels

start.description: Window start, unix epoch seconds. Keep windows under ~30 days; very wide windows fail in the metrics backend

step.description: Resolution step, e.g. '30s', '5m', '1h'; use larger steps for wider windows

recover_device.description: Recover a soft-deleted device/resource (requires write permission). Only works within the recovery window.

run_netscan.description: Execute a network scan (requires write permission)

run_portal_reload.description: Re-read the vault so portals added or removed since startup take effect without restarting the client.

search_tools.description: Search the tools this server offers under its current settings by keyword, optionally within one category. Use it to find the tool for a task. It never names a tool the settings hide, so with writes off no write tool appears. Words such as 'the' and 'on' are ignored, plurals match singulars, and a query word that is a tool's full name ranks that tool first.

set_action_rule_status.description: Enable or disable an action rule without touching its matchers (requires write permission)

enabled.description: True to enable, False to disable

set_session_variable.description: Set a user-defined session variable for use across tool calls

value.description: Variable value (string, number, boolean, array, or object)

terraform_generate.description: Export an existing LogicMonitor resource as Terraform HCL configuration using the logicmonitor/logicmonitor provider. Supports device, device_group, collector, alert_rule, escalation_chain, dashboard, datasource, sdt, website, role, and report_group resource types.

resource_type.description: LM resource type to export (device, device_group, collector, collector_group, alert_rule, escalation_chain, dashboard, dashboard_group, datasource, sdt, website, website_group, role, report_group)

triage.description: Triage the alerts of the last hours_back hours in one call. Reads the alert window once through analyze_alerts for its statistics, clusters (by device, datasource and signature), noise and changes, then counts the blast radius of up to three device clusters, largest first. Each count row gives the devices reached as neighbors and as dependents, how many of them have a critical alert open, and how many devices' neighbors could not be read; a website cluster gets none. detail_level=full adds the devices each blast radius reached. Use analyze_alerts for bursts or a single section, and analyze_blast_radius for one device.

update_action_rule.description: Update an action rule via PATCH; only provided fields are sent (requires write permission)

update_collector.description: Update a collector (requires write permission). Change group, description, failback, or escalation chain.

escalation_chain_id.description: Escalation chain ID for collector down alerts

update_collector_group.description: Update a collector group (requires write permission)

update_dashboard.description: Update an existing dashboard (requires write permission)

update_dashboard_group.description: Update a dashboard group (requires write permission)

update_device.description: Update an existing device/resource (requires write permission). Custom properties are merged with existing properties (not replaced).

update_device_eventsource.description: Update a device-level EventSource association (requires write permission). Use to enable or disable alerting for an EventSource on a specific device.

disable_alerting.description: Set true to disable alerting, false to enable

update_device_group.description: Update a device/resource group (requires write permission). Custom properties are merged with existing.

applies_to.description: New AppliesTo expression for dynamic membership

custom_properties.description: Custom properties to set/update (merged with existing)

disable_alerting.description: Disable alerting for all devices in this group

parent_id.description: New parent group ID (moves the group)

update_device_instance.description: Update a monitored instance on a device (requires write permission)

disable_alerting.description: Disable or enable alerting for this instance

stop_monitoring.description: Stop or resume monitoring for this instance

update_device_property.description: Update or create a device/resource property (requires write permission)

update_escalation_chain.description: Update an escalation chain (requires write permission)

destinations.description: Updated list of Chain objects. Same shape as on create: {type, period, stages}. See create_escalation_chain for the full Recipient shape and integration-routing form.

throttling_alerts.description: Updated number of alerts before throttling

update_http_integration.description: Update a Custom HTTP Delivery integration via PATCH. Only fields explicitly provided are sent; omitted fields keep their current server values. (requires write permission)

update_logicmodule.description: Update a LogicModule definition (configsource, datasource, diagnosticsource, eventsource, logsource, propertysource, remediationsource, topologysource). Reads the current full definition, deep-merges your `changes` onto it, validates required fields, and either returns a dry-run diff (mode='preview', default) or applies the merged definition (mode='apply'). The LogicMonitor update is full-replace, so the merged full definition is sent and fields you do not change are kept.

changes.description: Partial update -- only the fields to change. Use `null` as a value to explicitly delete a key. Lists replace wholesale.

mode.description: 'preview' returns a dry-run diff without writing (default). 'apply' writes the merged definition with a full-replace PUT.

update_ops_note.description: Update an ops note (requires write permission)

device_ids.description: New device IDs to scope the note to

group_ids.description: New device group IDs to scope the note to

update_recipient_group.description: Update a recipient group (requires write permission)

name.description: Updated name. Sent as groupName to the LM v3 API.

recipients.description: Replacement recipient list. When provided, LM replaces the group's current recipient set with this list.

update_report_schedule.description: Update a report's schedule (requires write permission)

enabled.description: Pass false to clear (disable) the schedule

update_sdt.description: Update a scheduled downtime (requires write permission). Uses fetch-modify-PUT to preserve unmodified fields.

end_date_time.description: New end time in epoch milliseconds

start_date_time.description: New start time in epoch milliseconds

update_user.description: Update a user in LogicMonitor (requires write permission)

update_website.description: Update a website check in LogicMonitor (requires write permission)

use_portal.description: Switch the active customer portal for subsequent tool calls.
